original_statement:
What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. With --follow-definition-changes, a valCompare body edit and the statement follow it needs are one candidate, attempted in one rebuild. Decision X7 and the S1c acceptance check of docs/parallel.md hold.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. A followStatement candidate is proposed for a statement site only after a body edit was accepted earlier in the run (Shell/Target.lean passes the followed list). The body edit and the statement edit are separate attempts. The branch s1-partial (commit 5885691) holds the captured work of the first S1 worker (lea-e1b), killed at the 3600-second task timeout. It builds, it has no sorry, and lake test reports 0 failed. It has Site.declIndex, Site.key, keyLt with its order theorems, Mending.sortOpens with its proofs, Mending.afterCoord, and a five-tuple Mending.measure. It has no tests/order.sh, no tests/expose.sh and no fixture.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. Run tests/follow-pair.sh on tests/fixtures/follow-pair, as docs/parallel.md S1c states: the ledger holds one attempt with both edits, and the Core accepts it. Run tests/follow.sh. Run scripts/gate.sh: stdout is one JSON object; its steps list holds a step named 'D12 body edit and statement follow as one candidate' with ok true, and failed is 0.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. Spec and Core import no Shell module (scripts/gate.sh checks it). Termination stays a theorem in LeanMend/Spec/Termination.lean, with no retry cap and no timeout as a control. Decision D10 holds: lean-mend adds no declaration to a target. lean-mend depends on Lean core only, not on Mathlib. Every committed text is in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Run export PATH="$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH" before a lean or lake command. Scratch files go in the gitignored .scratch/ directory, not /tmp. The worker task timeout is 3600 seconds. Do not run lean-mend on EVMLean: one EVMLean run takes about 2 hours, and the operator runs it after the merge.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) LeanMend/Core/Ops.lean, LeanMend/Core/Propose.lean, LeanMend/Shell/Target.lean
restatement: With --follow-definition-changes, lean-mend must treat a valCompare body edit and the statement follow edit it needs as ONE candidate, tried in ONE rebuild, so the earliest error never moves back (Decision X7, S1c of docs/parallel.md). The follow-pair test on tests/fixtures/follow-pair, the follow test and the gate must all show this. The design rules stay: Spec and Core import no Shell module, termination stays a theorem with no retry cap or timeout, and lean-mend depends on Lean core only.

The gate script defines the step named 'D12 body edit and statement follow as one candidate'.
